 Post published at 06:38 GMT 06:38 GMT 
 Australian fast bowler Mahli Beardman told TNT Sports: "My favourite wicket? The first one, Harry Brook, was a nice one to get off the mark. Any time you get your first it's a weight off your shoulders. 
 "I was pretty nervous early on. With my first ball I just tried to hit the cut stuff! I was a little bit worried, but once I got that one out the way everything started to feel pretty natural. It's been such a great group to be around and Mitch Marsh is such an incredible leader so that helped calm those nerves.
 "I think the key to bowling on this pitch is using seam angles. I think we were clear with our plans we just executed it. It's a privilege to bowl in this attack."

Former England captain on Test Match Special 
 Image source, Getty Images England's top order will look back on this and think about this kind of approach. They would have seen it was bouncing, and moving, which doesn't mean you go into your shell. But you can just let the bowlers have a few overs, because 50 overs is a long time to bat. 
 I guess it's in the DNA of these modern players - that they want to get on with it. If you want to win a World Cup, you need to adapt to conditions and England have not done that of late. But you can't have a car that goes straight from first gear to fifth. It needs to go through second, third and fourth.

 Australia need 132 to win published at 06:23 GMT 06:23 GMT 
 A disgrace, Robin? Or a valiant recovery from 65-8?
 OK, fair enough, no matter how you look at it, that is an innings England will not look back on too fondly.
 There was plenty in it for the Australia quicks and they bowled very well, debutant Mahli Beardman in particular, but England's batting left plenty to be desired.
 It'll take some bowling effort to make a game of it from here. To see if Jofra Archer and co can manage that, here's Timothy Abraham .

 WICKET published at 33.4 overs 33.4 overs 
 Archer c Edwards b Beardman 11 (Eng 131 all out) 
 Superb catch and Mahli Beardman has six on debut!
 Width, Jofra Archer tries to cash in but gets a thick edge and the ball flashes towards backward point.
 Jack Edwards is there and takes an excellent catch going to his left.
 Beardman ends with figures of 6-24, the best by an Australian on ODI debut, as England are rolled cheaply.

 How's stat?! published at 06:03 GMT 06:03 GMT 
 Josh Inglis has taken five catches in this innings, the second time he has done so in an ODI. The previous instance came in the World Cup final against India on 19 November 2023.
 Adam Gilchrist is the only Australian wicketkeeper to take six catches in an ODI, having achieved the feat on four occasions.

 Jofra Archer is away with a boundary!
 He uses the angle of Spencer Johnson and gets his cut shot away with just enough power to beat the fielder in the deep.

 Ah, Mahli Beardman is coming back on to try and add to his five wickets on ODI debut.

 England's morning of woe... published at 06:00 GMT 06:00 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images If you're just joining us... Australia's players are doing their best to get sandpaper out of the headlines. 
 England, meanwhile, are doing little to help themselves with another pitiful performance in Perth.
 This morning has been all about an exciting debutant by the name of Mahli Beardman.
 The 21-year-old bagged five wickets in his first five overs as England's top order folded quicker than competitors at a origami tournament.
 Asked to bat, the tourists lost both openers during a steady powerplay but have since been blown away.
 Beardman dismissed Harry Brook in his second over, added Joe Root in his next and has since accounted for Jordan Cox, Sam Curran and Liam Dawson in his maiden five-for.
 Gus Atkinson and Will Jacks eked out a few runs for the eighth wicket, hoping to nudge the tourists to some sort of total, before Spencer Johnson removed the latter just after drinks.
